text.p: Colgate-Palmolive Co., the global consumer products giant, Tuesday reported record profits for the fourth quarter despite the strong dollar, which hurt sales in Europe.
The company said it earned $181.7 million, or $1.20 a share, in the quarter, compared with year-earlier earnings of $122.5 million, or 80 cents a share.
Sales for the quarter rose 7 percent to $2.30 billion and would have risen 8 percent but for the stronger dollar, it said. In the fourth quarter of 1995, Colgate reported sales of $2.15 billion.

Colgate's stock rose $2 to $98.25 on the New York Stock Exchange, a 52-week high, on reports the company was bullish about its 1997 performance. It said it was comfortable with the range of $4.70 per share to $4.85 per share for the year.
"They seemed very comfortable with the range," said Michael Grant, a J.P. Morgan analyst. "It looks like they are poised for a very strong year."

Colgate said its profits set a record for the year at $635 million, or $4.19 a share, on sales of $8.74 billion. That compared with 1995 earnings of $172 million, or $1.04 a share, on sales of $8.35 billion.
The company's 1995 results included a massive rectructuring charge of $369.2 million.

"Colgate enters 1997 with excellent global momentum," said Chairman Reuben Mark. "Every operating division around the world achieved healthy unit volume growth in the fourth quarter, led by Colgate-North America, up 7 percent, and Colgate-Latin America, up 11 percent, highlighted by further recovery in Mexico."

The company, whose products include Colgate toothpaste, Palmolive soap, Ajax detergent and Speed Stick deodorant, said sales in North America rose 6 percent in the fourth quarter and were up 5 percent for the year, boosted by strong revenues from such products as Colgate Baking Soda & Peroxide toothpaste, Palmolive dishwashing liquid and antibacterial hand soap.
In Europe, Colgate said currency fluctuations hurt its fourth-quarter sales, which were off 1 percent, and for the full year European sales were flat with 1995.
Analysts said the company reiterated its strong showing in both top-line and margin growth during its conference call.
The company also told analysts it expected its Total toothpaste to be cleared for U.S. release in the second half of the year, perhaps in the third quarter.

The company has been waiting for the Food and Drug Administration to approve the marketing of Total as a treatment for gingivitis, plaque, tartar and cavities. It originally was expected at the end of 1996, then the first quarter of 1997.
Still, analysts said the company's results were promising.

"Results were solid across all divisions," Heather Hay, a Prudential Securities analyst, said in her research report. "Margins also continue to improve, even as Colgate ups their advertising efforts."
